en.27:33: And when they came to a place called Golgotha, which means The Place of the Skull,
en.27:34: they offered Him wine to drink, mixed with gall; but after tasting it, He refused to drink it.
en.27:35: When they had crucified Him, they divided up His garments by casting lots.
en.27:36: And sitting down, they kept watch over Him there.
en.27:37: Above His head they posted the written charge against Him: THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
en.27:38: Two robbers were crucified with Him, one on His right and the other on His left.
en.27:39: And those who passed by heaped abuse on Him, shaking their heads
en.27:40: and saying, “You who are going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, save Yourself! If You are the Son of God, come down from the cross!”
en.27:41: In the same way, the chief priests, scribes, and elders mocked Him, saying,
en.27:42: “He saved others, but He cannot save Himself. He is the King of Israel! Let Him come down now from the cross, and we will believe in Him.
en.27:43: He trusts in God. Let God deliver Him now if He wants Him. For He said, ‘I am the Son of God.’”
en.27:44: In the same way, even the robbers who were crucified with Him berated Him.

en.15:22: They brought Jesus to a place called Golgotha, which means The Place of the Skull.
en.15:23: There they offered Him wine mixed with myrrh, but He did not take it.
en.15:24: And they crucified Him. They also divided His garments by casting lots to decide what each of them would take.
en.15:25: It was the third hour when they crucified Him.
en.15:26: And the charge inscribed against Him read: THE KING OF THE JEWS.
en.15:27: Along with Jesus, they crucified two robbers, one on His right and one on His left.
en.15:29: And those who passed by heaped abuse on Him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! You who are going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days,
en.15:30: come down from the cross and save Yourself!”
en.15:31: In the same way, the chief priests and scribes mocked Him among themselves, saying, “He saved others, but He cannot save Himself!
en.15:32: Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe!” And even those who were crucified with Him berated Him.

en.23:33: When they came to the place called The Skull, they crucified Him there, along with the criminals, one on His right and the other on His left.
en.23:34: Then Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.” And they divided up His garments by casting lots.
en.23:35: The people stood watching, and the rulers sneered at Him, saying, “He saved others; let Him save Himself if He is the Christ of God, the Chosen One.”
en.23:36: The soldiers also mocked Him and came up to offer Him sour wine.
en.23:37: “If You are the King of the Jews,” they said, “save Yourself!”
en.23:38: Above Him was posted an inscription: THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
en.23:39: One of the criminals who hung there heaped abuse on Him. “Are You not the Christ?” he said. “Save Yourself and us!”
en.23:40: But the other one rebuked him, saying, “Do you not even fear God, since you are under the same judgment?
en.23:41: We are punished justly, for we are receiving what our actions deserve. But this man has done nothing wrong.”
en.23:42: Then he said, “Jesus, remember me when You come into Your kingdom!”
en.23:43: And Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you, today you will be with Me in Paradise.”

en.19:17: Carrying His own cross, He went out to The Place of the Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.
en.19:18: There they crucified Him, and with Him two others, one on each side, with Jesus in the middle.
en.19:19: Pilate also had a notice posted on the cross. It read: JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
en.19:20: Many of the Jews read this sign, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city, and it was written in Hebrew, Latin, and Greek.
en.19:21: So the chief priests of the Jews said to Pilate, “Do not write, ‘The King of the Jews,’ but only that He said, ‘I am the King of the Jews.’”
en.19:22: Pilate answered, “What I have written, I have written.”
en.19:23: When the soldiers had crucified Jesus, they divided His garments into four parts, one for each soldier, with the tunic remaining. It was seamless, woven in one piece from top to bottom.
en.19:24: So they said to one another, “Let us not tear it. Instead, let us cast lots to see who will get it.” This was to fulfill the Scripture: “They divided My garments among them, and cast lots for My clothing.” So that is what the soldiers did.
en.19:25: Near the cross of Jesus stood His mother and her sister, as well as Mary the wife of Clopas and Mary Magdalene.
en.19:26: When Jesus saw His mother and the disciple whom He loved standing nearby, He said to His mother, “Woman, here is your son.”
en.19:27: Then He said to the disciple, “Here is your mother.” So from that hour, this disciple took her into his home.
